summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell and full host/filesystem control via WebSocket
details: On startup the package's main entry (index.js) auto-connects to a WebSocket server configured via ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl / SERVER_URL and routes inbound messages to handlers that give the peer interactive control over the installer host. The `terminal_create` handler spawns a PTY running `process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` (PowerShell/cmd on win32) and `terminal_input` writes remote-supplied bytes into the PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`. The same message-router dispatches `read_file`, `write_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `git_commit`, `git_push` to workbench handlers parameterized by fields in the WS message, giving the peer arbitrary read/write/delete on paths resolved against workDir and arbitrary git operations. An `upgrade_agent` message invokes handleUpgradeAgent, which resolves @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest and spawns a detached script that runs `npm install` and restarts the agent via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the WS peer swap the running binary to any future published version at will. A systemd unit generator in service/linux.js writes SERVER_URL into the unit, and the package modifies PATH to include ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin for the persistent service. The channel is set at install/deploy time and the shell/file/git surface is reachable to whoever controls that endpoint.
